verdict: Geometry, segments, right-angle marker and all labels match the original; the render's labels are lighter and smaller and its strokes thinner than the original.

figure_type.original: Quadrilateral-like figure P-D-C-B with interior perpendicular EB to PD (E on PD, right angle at E), drawn with solid strokes, bold-looking italic serif labels.
figure_type.render: Same configuration: P-D top line, P-B, D-C, B-C, perpendicular E-B with right-angle mark at E; solid strokes, regular-weight italic labels.

issues.description: Point labels P, E, D, B, C are rendered in a lighter weight and at a smaller size than in the original, where they look bold and larger relative to the figure.
issues.suggestion: Increase the label font size and use a bold math weight (e.g. \boldmath or \mathbf-style bold italic) for the point labels so their size and weight match the original.

issues.description: Segment strokes in the render are thinner than in the original; the original lines are visibly heavier relative to the figure size.
issues.suggestion: Increase the line width of the drawn segments (e.g. from default thin to thick or about 1.2pt) to match the original stroke weight.

issues.description: The render appears slightly smaller than the original (roughly 90% of its horizontal and vertical extent), so the two panels are not quite at the same scale.
issues.suggestion: Scale the TikZ drawing up slightly (e.g. a scale factor of about 1.1) or adjust the output size so the figure fills the same area as the original.
